review_comments.body:
### Duplicate `downsize` method breaks existing emoji resizing caller **High Severity** Two `downsize` class methods are defined on `OptimizedImage`. In Ruby, the second definition (3-arg: `from, to, dimensions`) completely replaces the first (4-arg: `from, to, max_width, max_height`). The existing caller in `resize_emoji.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, which will raise an `ArgumentError` at runtime since the surviving signature only accepts 3–4 arguments.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/models/optimized_image.rb#L144-L147`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896/app/models/optimized_image.rb#L144-L147)

### Hardcoded file size limit ignores site settings and type **Medium Severity** The client-side max upload size is hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, replacing the dynamic lookup from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This removes per-type (`image` vs `attachment`) validation and ignores admin-configured site settings. Non-image uploads (attachments) now bypass their actual size limit on the client, only to be rejected server-side with a confusing error, since auto-downsizing only applies to images.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js#L245-L246`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896/app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js#L245-L246)

### Percentage dimensions incompatible with gifsicle for animated GIFs **Medium Severity** The auto-downsize loop passes `"80%"` as dimensions and explicitly sets `allow_animation`, intending to support animated GIFs. However, for animated GIFs (matching `\.GIF$/i`), the code path goes through `resize_instructions_animated` which invokes `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle expects pixel-based `WxH` dimensions, not percentages. This causes the downsize to fail silently on every iteration, the loop runs all 5 attempts doing nothing, and oversized animated GIFs are never reduced.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/models/optimized_image.rb#L114-L123`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/ffbaf8c54269df2ce510de91245760fddce09896/app/models/optimized_image.rb#L114-L123)

prs.title: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails

review_comments.body: ### Nil dereference when TopicUser record doesn't exist **High Severity** `TopicUser.find_by` returns `nil` when no record exists for the given user and topic. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level` without a nil check, which will raise a `NoMethodError`. This is easily triggered — a user could receive a notification email (e.g., via mention) for a topic they've never visited, meaning no `TopicUser` record exists yet.

### GET unsubscribe changes state on every page load **Medium Severity** The `unsubscribe` action mutates `TopicUser` notification level on every GET request. A user at "watching" level gets downgraded to "regular" on first load; refreshing the page then changes it to "muted". This double-step degradation on page refresh is almost certainly unintended. Additionally, email client link prefetching can silently trigger the state change before the user even clicks.
Additional Locations (1) - [`config/routes.rb#L439-L441`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/6669a2d94d76eea3b99b8c476d12b1eb66726b07/config/routes.rb#L439-L441)

prs.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

review_comments.body:
### Validation side effect causes double-counted blocked email matches **Medium Severity** `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a database write (incrementing `match_count` and updating `last_match_at`) every time it's called. Because it's invoked from within `EmailValidator#validate_each`, and the user creation flow in `users_controller.rb` calls `user.valid?` explicitly before `user.save` (which runs validations again internally), the counter gets incremented twice per account creation attempt. Placing database side effects inside a validation method breaks the expectation that validation is idempotent and read-only.
Additional Locations (1) - [`lib/validators/email_validator.rb#L12-L15`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213/lib/validators/email_validator.rb#L12-L15)

### Case-sensitive lookup lets users bypass blocked emails **Medium Severity** `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a case-sensitive database lookup via `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`. Since Discourse uses PostgreSQL (case-sensitive string comparison by default) and the `email` column is a plain `string` type, a user can bypass a blocked email entry like "bad@spam.com" by registering with "Bad@Spam.com". This is inconsistent with `email_in_restriction_setting?` in the same `EmailValidator`, which uses a case-insensitive regex for whitelist/blacklist matching.

prs.title: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

review_comments.body: ### ERB template uses `end if` without condition expression **High Severity** `<%- end if %>` uses `end if` (a Ruby modifier `if`) without a condition expression instead of just `end`. Depending on the ERB compiler, this either causes a syntax error (template fails to compile) or accidentally captures the next ERB output statement as the `if` condition — making the entire if/else block conditional on a side-effectful buffer write. Either way, the embed best view is broken or behaves incorrectly.

### RSS item `content` may be nil causing crash **Medium Severity** `i.content.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError` when `i.content` is `nil`. Standard RSS 2.0 feeds use `description` rather than `content` (which comes from the `content:encoded` extension or Atom feeds). SimpleRSS returns `nil` for missing item fields, so any standard RSS feed without a `content` element will crash the scheduled polling job.

### Method `feed_key` defined but never called anywhere **Low Severity** The `feed_key` method generates a Redis key string using the feed URL's SHA1 hash, but it is never called within `PollFeed` or anywhere else in the codebase. This appears to be leftover code from an incomplete implementation of feed modification tracking.

### Origin validation uses permissive substring check **Low Severity** `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` checks whether `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`, rather than performing a strict origin comparison. An attacker controlling a domain that is a prefix of the Discourse URL (e.g., `http://discourse.co` vs `http://discourse.com`) would pass this check and could send accepted `postMessage` events to manipulate the iframe height.

prs.title: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins

review_comments.body:
### Button loses right alignment in new flex container **Medium Severity** Adding `flexbox()` to `.small-action` causes `float: right` on the child `button` to be silently ignored — per the CSS spec, float has no effect on flex items. The button previously floated to the far right but now just appears inline after the other items. In `header.scss`, the same issue for `.panel` was correctly handled by adding `margin-left: auto`, but no equivalent fix was applied here.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss#L305-L310`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/5b229316ee4c661836ed1161139692a3e8527444/app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss#L305-L310)

### Order mixin has off-by-one for older webkit **Low Severity** The `order` mixin passes `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but those legacy properties use 1-based indexing (default: 1), while standard `order` uses 0-based indexing (default: 0). The legacy properties need `$val + 1` to produce equivalent ordering behavior. For the values currently used (2, 3) the relative ordering happens to be preserved, but it would break for values like 0 or 1.

### Mobile custom message overflows due to stale margin offset **Medium Severity** The base `.small-action-desc` padding changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, but the mobile stylesheet still has `.custom-message { margin-left: -40px; }` which was designed to offset the old `4em` (~64px) left padding. With only `1.5%` left padding remaining, the `-40px` margin now causes `.custom-message` to overflow significantly to the left, likely overlapping the avatar on mobile devices.

prs.title: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain

review_comments.body: ### Missing `?` suffix on conditional include method **High Severity** The method `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` that ActiveModel::Serializer requires for conditional attribute inclusion. Every other conditional include method in this file uses the `?` suffix (e.g., `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_stats?`). Without it, the serializer never calls this method, so `website_name` is always included in the serialized output — even when `website` is blank.

### Website name leaks for restricted TL0 user profiles **Medium Severity** The `website` attribute is registered as an `untrusted_attributes` entry, which hides it from anonymous users viewing TL0 profiles. However, the new `website_name` attribute (derived from `website`) is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, so it will still be serialized for those users, leaking the website information that was intentionally hidden.

### Subdomain matching wrongly matches unrelated ccTLD domains **Low Severity** The subdomain comparison logic strips only the first segment and compares the remainder. This incorrectly treats completely unrelated domains sharing a country-code TLD as matching — e.g., `evil.co.uk` and `good.co.uk` would match because `co.uk == co.uk`, causing the full URL path to be displayed when it shouldn't be.

prs.title: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes

review_comments.body: ### Light theme lightness value changed from 30% to 70% **Medium Severity** The `.topic-meta-data h5 a` color for light themes was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The first argument to `dark-light-choose` (the light theme value) should preserve the original `30%` lightness, but it was accidentally set to `70%`. This makes the link text significantly lighter/washed-out on light themes.

### Mobile modal light/dark theme values are swapped **Medium Severity** The `.custom-message-length` color has its light and dark theme lightness values swapped compared to the desktop equivalent. The original was `$lightness: 70%`, and the desktop version correctly uses `70%` for light / `30%` for dark. The mobile version incorrectly uses `30%` for light / `70%` for dark, making the text much darker on light themes and lighter on dark themes than intended.

### Mobile h3 light theme lightness changed from 20% to 50% **Medium Severity** The `h3` element's light theme lightness was changed from `20%` to `50%`, making it noticeably lighter. The desktop equivalent at `desktop/topic-post.scss` correctly preserves `20%` for light and uses `80%` for dark. The mobile version appears to have lost the original value, making the heading text less prominent on light themes than intended.

### Group member name light theme lightness changed from 30% **Low Severity** The `.group-member-info .name` color's light theme lightness was changed from `30%` to `50%` in both desktop and mobile stylesheets. The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the correct transformation would keep `30%` for light and use `70%` for dark. This makes the group member name text lighter/less prominent on light themes than originally intended.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss#L496-L497`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38/app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss#L496-L497)

prs.title: FIX: proper handling of group memberships

review_comments.body: ### Incorrect pagination calculation causes extra empty page **Medium Severity** The `totalPages` calculation uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which incorrectly adds an extra page when `user_count` is evenly divisible by `limit`. For example, with 100 users and limit 50, it returns 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty third page. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

### Promise chain breaks when group name is empty **High Severity** The `findMembers()` method returns `undefined` when the group name is empty, breaking promise chains. The controller actions `next` and `previous` both return the result of `findMembers()`, expecting a promise. When the name is empty, this returns `undefined` instead, causing errors when code tries to call `.then()` on the undefined value.

### Inconsistent member removal bypasses model method **Low Severity** The `remove_member` action uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` to remove members, while `add_members` uses `group.add(user)`. This inconsistency bypasses the `group.remove(user)` method which properly destroys GroupUser join records via `group_users.where(user: user).each(&:destroy)`. The direct association manipulation might skip important cleanup logic.

### Pagination offset calculation allows empty page display **Low Severity** The `next` action caps the offset at `user_count` instead of the last valid offset. When `user_count` equals a multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), clicking next from the second-to-last page sets offset to 100, causing the API to request items 100-149 when only 0-99 exist, returning zero results and displaying an empty page to the user.

### Usernames with spaces silently fail to add members **Medium Severity** The `add_members` action splits usernames by comma but doesn't strip whitespace from each username before lookup. When users enter "user1, user2" (with space after comma), it attempts to find " user2" with a leading space, which fails to match the actual username "user2". These usernames are silently skipped without any error feedback to the user.

### Missing error handling causes silent add/remove failures **Medium Severity** The `removeMember` and `addMembers` actions call model methods that return promises but don't handle failures. When API calls fail due to network errors, validation errors, or server issues, users receive no feedback that the operation failed. The member list isn't reloaded on failure, leaving the UI showing stale data while the user believes the operation succeeded.
Additional Locations (1) - [`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6#L63-L64`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/060cda77729cb1c4a827560e09e89a7b22078ba9/app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6#L63-L64)

### Invalid page displayed after membership count changes **Medium Severity** After adding or removing members, `findMembers()` updates `user_count` from the server but doesn't validate or reset the `offset`. When viewing page 3 (offset=100) of a group with 150 members and members are removed such that only 50 remain, the offset stays at 100, leaving the user on an invalid empty page showing "page 3 of 1" with no results displayed.

prs.title: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding

review_comments.body: ### Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent **High Severity** The migration unconditionally accesses `[0]['id']` on the result of the `embed_category` query. If `embed_category` was never configured (common for many installations), the query returns zero rows, `[0]` returns `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises a `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration. The code at line 14 intends to handle this case with a fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, but execution never reaches it because the crash happens first.

### Case-sensitive host comparison defeats case-insensitive intent **Medium Severity** In `record_for_host`, the SQL query uses `lower(host)` on the database column but doesn't lowercase the `host` parameter parsed from the URI. Ruby's `URI` preserves the original casing of hostnames, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com` would fail to match because `lower(db_column)` yields `"eviltrout.com"` but the bound parameter remains `"EvilTrout.com"`. The parameter needs to be downcased too.

### SQL injection via unsanitized host value interpolation **Medium Severity** The migration uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert host values directly into a raw SQL `INSERT` statement. Since these values come from user-configured `embeddable_hosts` site settings, a malicious or unexpected value containing a single quote could break the query or allow SQL injection. Parameterized queries or proper escaping with `quote` would be safer.

### String replace only affects first underscore in type **Low Severity** `type.replace('_', '-')` in `basePath` only replaces the first underscore because JavaScript's `String.prototype.replace` with a string argument doesn't use global replacement. Any future model type with multiple underscores would fail to match in `ADMIN_MODELS`. A regex like `/_/g` would be correct for all cases.

### Fabricator definitions placed in wrong files **Low Severity** The file contents appear to have been swapped. `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricator definitions (`Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is confusing and will mislead anyone looking for fabricator definitions by filename convention.
Additional Locations (1) - [`spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb#L1-L27`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-discourse/blob/d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19/spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb#L1-L27)
